title: VoIP-Pal Files Third Amended Complaint Against AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile in Federal Antitrust Action
author: Voip-Pal.Com Inc.
description: VoIP-Pal filed a Third Amended Complaint in federal court against AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile, alleging antitrust violations under the Sherman Act. The complaint claims the carriers unlawfully condition Wi-Fi calling access on purchasing their cellular plans, foreclosing the market for independent Wi-Fi calling providers.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Named defendant in antitrust complaint alleging unlawful tying practices and monopoly maintenance through conditioning Wi-Fi calling access on cellular plan purchases.

title: AST SpaceMobile vs. Space Exploration Technologies: Which Telecom Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Brendan Coffey
description: AST SpaceMobile and SpaceX compete in satellite connectivity but with different business models. AST SpaceMobile focuses on direct-to-device smartphone connectivity with partnerships from major telecom operators, while SpaceX leverages reusable rockets to scale its Starlink broadband service. Despite SpaceX's larger revenue base ($18.7B vs $70.9M) and established business, the article recommends AST SpaceMobile for 2026 due to strong telecom backing and clearer near-term profitability path, though both companies face significant cash burn and execution risks.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Recommended as the better buy for 2026 due to strong backing from major telecom operators (AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, etc.), clear path to profitability by 2027, and expected revenue acceleration once 45-satellite constellation is deployed by end of 2026. Despite current losses and negative free cash flow, the company has supportive equity holders and manageable capital requirements compared to SpaceX.

While SpaceX has an established Starlink business with $18.7B revenue and operates profitably in some segments, the article raises concerns about muddled mission focus (telecom vs. cargo vs. Mars colonization), massive negative free cash flow projections ($28-67B), and unclear path to sustained profitability. The company is reasonably valued but faces execution risks and strategic ambiguity.

title: Why Is SpaceX (SPCX) Up 30% Since Last Earnings Report?
author: Na
description: SpaceX reported Q2 2026 earnings that beat estimates with a narrower loss of 9 cents per share versus 26 cents expected. Revenue surged 91.9% to $7.81 billion, driven by AI cloud services and Starlink expansion which doubled to 12 million subscribers. The company posted adjusted EBITDA of $3.54 billion and targets over $100 billion in annualized revenue run rate by year-end, though high capital expenditures of $18.37 billion and segment losses in Space operations remain concerns.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Strong earnings beat with 91.9% revenue growth, significant margin expansion in Connectivity segment (38.6%), AI segment profitability reversal, doubled Starlink subscribers to 12 million, and upward estimate revisions (129.53%). Stock gained 30% in past month and received Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) rating. However, tempered by high capex spending and Space segment losses.

Modest revenue growth of 2.3% year-over-year, EPS improvement from $0.54 to $0.65, and positive earnings guidance (+14.8% expected). However, stock gained only 12.5% in past month compared to SpaceX's 30%, and received Zacks Rank #3 (Hold) rating with unchanged consensus estimates over 30 days.

title: AST Spacemobile Just Moved Its Commercial Launch Target to 2027. Is That Bad News for Its Stock?
author: Leo Sun
description: AST SpaceMobile pushed back its target of deploying 45 satellites from late 2026 to early 2027, disappointing investors and contributing to a stock decline from a record high of $133.09 to the low $60s. Despite the delay caused by the loss of BlueBird 7 in April, the company maintains strong fundamentals including partnerships with 60+ carriers, a $1.3 billion backlog, and analyst projections showing revenue growth from $71 million in 2025 to $1.73 billion by 2028.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed signals: negative near-term due to delayed satellite deployment targets and stock decline from $133 to $62, but positive long-term outlook with strong partnerships (60+ carriers), substantial backlog ($1.3B), and analyst projections showing significant revenue growth through 2028. The article suggests the pullback could represent a buying opportunity for long-term investors.

title: Why Is AST SpaceMobile Stock Up 13% Today?
author: Johnny Rice
description: AST SpaceMobile stock surged 13% on September 2, 2026, after Berenberg initiated coverage with a Buy rating and set a $92 price target, implying 51% upside. The bank believes AST can build a profitable satellite network using a direct-to-device model complementary to terrestrial carriers like Verizon and AT&T. However, the company faces significant execution risk with a $230.9 million net loss last quarter, despite $31.5 million in revenue, and carries $3 billion in long-term debt against $2.7 billion in cash.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Positive analyst initiation with Buy rating and 51% upside price target from Berenberg, reflecting confidence in the company's satellite network commercialization and complementary business model with major carriers.
